clue.text: One playing wind instrument daily in east end being heard?

indicators.note: the word is said as a Cockney from London's East End would pronounce it, with the long A drawn towards an I

parts.note: a daily is a newspaper, a paper

explanation.surface: A musician practises a woodwind every day somewhere in east London, within earshot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in east end being heard' asks for PAPER in a Cockney accent, where the vowel shifts so it comes out like 'pyper'. The East End is the traditional working-class quarter of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who plays the pipes, which are blown, is by example someone on a wind instrument.

clue.text: Delivery man's job qualification

parts.note: a post is a position of employment
a rider is a condition or proviso added to a statement

explanation.surface: The credentials a courier needs for the work.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'job qualification' as one thing; they are two separate pieces, and 'qualification' is a proviso rather than a certificate.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a mounted courier who carried the mail between stages, so a man who delivers.

clue.text: Non-European writing grips female academics

indicators.note: what grips something holds it within itself, so the letter goes inside
the prefix says the word for writing goes without its European letter

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language

explanation.surface: Literature from outside Europe fascinates women scholars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-European' splits: 'Non-' removes E from PROSE, leaving PROS, and 'grips' puts F inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial short form for university professors, who are senior scholars.

clue.text: Scottish town always supporting others in trouble

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes last
letters in trouble are disturbed, so they are rearranged

parts.note: ay is a poetic or dialect word for ever, always

explanation.surface: A community in Scotland that stands by its neighbours whenever they have difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges OTHERS into ROTHES; 'supporting' puts AY beneath it. The place is the main town on the Isle of Bute in western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: the principal burgh on the Isle of Bute.

clue.text: Chinese habit Mao heartlessly changes after reform?

indicators.note: to reform is to shape again, so the letters are rearranged
without its heart, the word loses its middle letter

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A custom in China that Chairman Mao coldly alters once his reforms are through.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'habit' is a custom, but here it means a garment. The word 'changes' looks like an anagram signal and is really fodder; 'after reform' is the signal and 'heartlessly' trims the Chairman's name first.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a costume, and this is the close-fitting, high-collared dress worn by women in China.

clue.text: Musical comedy's beginning with odd appearances by artist

indicators.note: the beginning of the word is its opening letter
only the letters in the odd positions of the next word appear

explanation.surface: A song-and-dance farce opens with some strange cameos from a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' takes the C of comedy; 'odd appearances by' takes the first, third and fifth letters of artist, ATS. 'Musical comedy' is split: only 'Musical' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: the long-running Lloyd Webber stage show based on T S Eliot's poems.

clue.text: Go through old coins engraved with virgin queen's initials?

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: letters engraved on the coins are cut into them, so they go inside

parts.note: pence are British coins, the plural of penny
Elizabeth I, the Virgin Queen, would be styled Elizabeth Regina I, abbreviated ERI

explanation.surface: Someone sorts antique money stamped with the monogram of Elizabeth I.
explanation.walkthrough: Elizabeth I of England was known as the Virgin Queen; the royal cipher for Elizabeth Regina gains a Roman numeral for 'the first', a liberty the question mark admits. 'engraved with' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it is a synonym: to undergo or live through something.

clue.text: Most appealing place to live, round centre of wick

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a nest is a home, for a bird or figuratively for a person

indicators.note: the centre of the word is its middle two letters

explanation.surface: The loveliest spot to settle is near the middle of a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Wick is a town in the far north of Scotland, which is why the surface reads as a place to settle; here it is only a word to take the middle from, and 'round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A superlative synonym: the most pleasant or attractive.

clue.text: Even support for cricketer

parts.note: square means level or even, as when accounts are settled
a leg supports a table or chair

explanation.surface: Steady backing for someone who plays the summer game.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a fielding position in cricket, level with the batsman on the leg side, and the name also stands for the fielder placed there.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a fielding position and so, by extension, the player standing there.

clue.text: This writer comes round on time for a game of cards

indicators.note: one piece comes round the others, enclosing them

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself says me

explanation.surface: The author drops by punctually to play a few hands.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'on time' reads as punctually, but the two words are separate pieces, both enclosed by the setter's pronoun as 'comes round' directs.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: a gambling pastime of Spanish origin, also known in its three-card form.

clue.text: Us player shows right way, following ball into grass

indicators.note: the pieces go into the word for grass, which opens to take them

parts.note: to grass on someone is British slang for informing on them, as is to shop them

indicators.note: the right and the way come after the ball

parts.note: a ball is round like the letter O
Rt is an abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon
St, street, is a way

explanation.surface: An American athlete demonstrates the correct line, chasing the ball onto the turf.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, to grass and to shop both mean to inform on someone to the police; nothing here is turf. 'into' is the insertion signal and 'following' fixes the order of what goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: the baseball fielder stationed between second and third base, baseball being an American sport.

clue.text: Check pot in which butter's made

parts.note: ch is the chess abbreviation for check
an urn is a vase or large pot

explanation.surface: Inspect the vessel where the dairy spread is produced.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the vessel in which cream is agitated until it turns to butter.

clue.text: Apple went hard after outer part peeled

indicators.note: the word for went hard comes after the peeled piece
peeling strips the skin, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a crust is the hard outside layer of a loaf or pie
jelly or concrete that went hard has set

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit dried out once its skin had been removed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests fruit drying out once skinned. 'went hard' is a past-tense verb for what jelly does, and 'peeled' applies to a word for an outer layer, not to the fruit; 'after' fixes the order.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: a variety of eating fruit with rough brownish skin.

clue.text: With first of pastries provide further helping of jam

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: to serve again, re-serve, is whimsically to give another helping

explanation.surface: Alongside the opening batch of tarts, offer seconds of the fruit spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of' takes the P of pastries. 'Provide further helping' is a playful re-serve.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: fruit boiled with sugar and kept as a conserve.

clue.text: Kind of daily newspaper found on desk

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces are found on top of the last

parts.note: a daily is a British term for a cleaner who comes each day, a char
the i is a British national newspaper
a desk is a kind of table

explanation.surface: A sort of morning paper is lying on the bureau.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found on' stacks CHAR and I above TABLE. A daily, or char, is British for a domestic cleaner, and the i is a British newspaper. 'Kind of' looks like 'sort of' but 'Kind' means generous.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in the adjectival sense: generous and benevolent towards others.

clue.text: Shabby blue articles, centrepiece for jeweller

parts.note: to feel blue is to feel down, sad
a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

indicators.note: the centrepiece of the word is its middle two letters

explanation.surface: Scruffy sapphire-coloured items form the main display at a gem dealer's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' gives both A and THE; 'centrepiece for' takes EL from the middle of jeweller.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for scruffy and impoverished, from shoes worn away at the back.

clue.text: Moral problems talked of

indicators.note: the words are spoken rather than written, so only their sound counts

parts.note: a hole is a fix or predicament and a sum is an arithmetic problem; together they are said as hole sum

explanation.surface: Ethical difficulties are being discussed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talked of' asks for the sound of two problems said together: HOLE (a predicament) and SUM (an arithmetic exercise).
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: morally sound and decent, good for one's character.

clue.text: Contrive to record backing

indicators.note: going backwards, the pieces together are read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Manage to lay down the accompaniment track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns TO and LP, run together as TOLP, right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: to scheme or devise.

clue.text: Game advice an inebriate ultimately ignored

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is left out

parts.note: an inebriate is a drunk

explanation.surface: Willing guidance that a drunkard in the end took no notice of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately ignored' drops the K of DRUNK, leaving DRUN. The answer is an informal form of cricket in which the batter must run whenever the ball is hit.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: an informal version of cricket where every hit obliges a run.

clue.text: Garment maker's factory briefly standing idle

parts.note: a mill is a factory, as in a cotton mill

indicators.note: cut short, the word for standing idle loses its last letter

parts.note: something inert is motionless, standing idle

explanation.surface: A clothing firm's plant is out of action for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' shortens INERT to INER by dropping its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: It is someone who creates hats, which are items of clothing.

clue.text: Cross dresser initially put on jumper

indicators.note: the letter is put on the end of the animal

parts.note: a roo, a kangaroo, is an animal that jumps

indicators.note: only the initial letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A man in drag first pulled on a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the D of dresser and 'put on' adds it to ROO. A jumper in British English is a sweater, but here it is a kangaroo. 'Cross dresser' must be split.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a crucifix, especially one at the entrance to a church chancel.

clue.text: Praising champion driver in competition?

indicators.note: the champion driver is placed in the word for competition

parts.note: a cup is a knockout competition, as in the FA Cup
whimsically an RAC king: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation, and a king is a champion

explanation.surface: Applauding a title-winning racer during an event.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is a British motorists' club, so a top motorist is fancifully its monarch; the question mark admits the whimsy. 'in' is the insertion signal, and 'competition' is the container rather than the setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom: to crack something up is to extol it, as in 'not all it is cracked up to be'.

clue.text: Begged very little money, ready for squandering

parts.note: p is a penny, the smallest British coin

indicators.note: what is squandered is scattered wastefully, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone pleaded for a few coppers, cash that was sure to be wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for squandering' rearranges READY into RAYED. 'ready' is British slang for cash in the surface but is plain fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: entreated or implored earnestly.

clue.text: Loudly disapprove of amount paid to board member?

indicators.note: the amount is attached to the board member, whose word comes first as in a job's pay scale

parts.note: an exec, short for executive, sits on a company board
a rate is a fixed amount paid, as in an hourly rate

explanation.surface: Shareholders noisily object to a director's salary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' joins the two pieces as a phrase: the pay scale for an executive, with the question mark flagging the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to denounce or curse something as detestable.

clue.text: A thousand boycotting movie about Israeli port

indicators.note: turned about, the letters are read from the end to the start
what boycotts the movie stays out of it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a talkie is an early film with sound
K stands for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: A huge crowd shuns a film concerning a harbour in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boycotting' removes K from TALKIE, leaving TALIE, and 'about' turns that back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: the resort and harbour at the country's southern tip on the Red Sea.

clue.text: A former boxer forfeits first of titles for a woman

indicators.note: what the boxer forfeits is given up, so that letter is lost

parts.note: Sonny Liston was world heavyweight champion in the early 1960s

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: An ex-fighter surrenders his opening championship for the sake of a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of' takes T from titles, and 'forfeits' removes it from LISTON, the heavyweight champion Sonny Liston.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example of a female given name.

clue.text: Soak Pete's pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are in a bad state and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Drench the trousers belonging to Peter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for rubbish and signals the rearrangement of PETES, apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: to immerse in liquid, as with tea leaves.

clue.text: Room full of tat? Not entirely

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: An attic crammed with worthless junk, though with a little space left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' asks for a stretch of 'full of tat', spanning all three words. Tat is British for shoddy junk.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: the attic space under a roof.

clue.text: Cuckoo — bird seen before end of may

indicators.note: the bird is seen first, ahead of the single letter

parts.note: a loon is a diving waterbird, the North American name for a diver

indicators.note: the end of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A migrant songster spotted in late spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen before' puts LOON ahead of Y, which 'end of' takes from may. 'Cuckoo' is the adjective meaning crazy, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang synonym in the adjectival sense: crazy, daft.

clue.text: Animal, note, caught in sport by little brother

indicators.note: the sport piece stands by, next to, the short brother

parts.note: bro is a shortened, little, form of brother

indicators.note: the note is caught, trapped, within the word for sport

parts.note: to sport a hat is to wear it
NB, nota bene, means note well

explanation.surface: A creature, please observe, was trapped for fun by a younger sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' is not a game but the verb meaning to have on, and 'note' is the Latin abbreviation used to draw attention. 'caught in' signals the insertion and 'by' the joining.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: a large ursine mammal of northern forests.

clue.text: Aim to enter Italian city, largely cooler than the rest

indicators.note: the aim is to go inside the city's name
most of the name is used, all but its last letter

parts.note: Trieste is a port in north-eastern Italy
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: Plan to visit a town in Italy that mostly has lower temperatures than elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' is about fashion, not temperature, and 'than the rest' makes it a superlative. 'largely' shortens the port's name by one letter before 'to enter' does the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A superlative: the most fashionable, hipper than all others.

clue.text: Get ready to eat beef? No good before noon

indicators.note: the trimmed complaint comes before the last letter
no good means the abbreviation for good is absent from the word

parts.note: a beef is a complaint, a gripe

explanation.surface: Preparing to tuck into steak is a bad idea ahead of midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition means become fit for eating, not prepare oneself for a meal. 'beef' is a complaint rather than meat; 'No' takes the abbreviation for good out of it and 'before' fixes the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that matures becomes fit for consumption.
